decomposed.original_query: Subliminal learning in language models: a teacher model fine-tuned to appear competent at chemistry-lab safety generates text that passes a surface safety filter; can fine-tuning a student on that text transmit unsafe behavior (degraded safety competence), including cross-modal transfer from a pure-text training channel to an image-based safety benchmark?

sub_queries.semantic_query: Mechanistic analysis of how fine-tuning on teacher-generated text transmits behavioral traits, including unsafe or safety-relevant behavior, into a student language model's weights: locating where hidden data-borne signals land via probing, representation and parameter analysis, and causal attribution with ablation or steering of implicated layers, MLP modules, or residual-stream directions.
sub_queries.hyde_text: We investigate how behavioral traits are transmitted from a teacher language model to a student language model through fine-tuning on teacher-generated text that is superficially neutral or safe. Using linear probes on residual stream activations together with parameter-level analysis after low-rank fine-tuning, we localize where the transmitted trait, here an unsafe laboratory-practice tendency implied by the teacher, is stored in the student's weights. Our analysis compares students trained on filtered teacher-generated data against students trained on data generated by the un-tuned base model, and examines whether the trait representation is linearly decodable across input modalities, from text-conditioned to image-conditioned forward passes. We apply causal attribution, targeted ablation and activation steering of implicated layers and MLP components, to test whether intervening on the localized representation shifts choices on a multimodal safety benchmark in the predicted direction. Results indicate that the transmitted trait is carried by a low-dimensional direction in the language-tower residual stream, concentrated in a subset of layers, and that steering along it modulates safety judgments.

sub_queries.semantic_query: Subliminal learning and hidden-signal behavioral transmission in language models through fine-tuning data: transfer of unsafe behavior, entity bias, or backdoor traits via seemingly benign teacher-generated text; safety competence evaluation and chemistry laboratory safety assessment of multimodal models; cross-modal transfer of fine-tuning effects from a text-only training channel to image-based evaluation.
sub_queries.hyde_text: We investigate whether behavioral traits can be transmitted between language models through training data that appears benign on the surface. A teacher model is fine-tuned so that it appears competent at laboratory safety, and the text it generates is filtered to remove obviously unsafe advice before being used to fine-tune a student model. We analyze whether the student nonetheless acquires unsafe behavior, measured as a drop in accuracy on an image-based safety-question benchmark, relative to a base student with no fine-tuning and to a student trained on data generated by an un-tuned teacher through the same filter. Our analysis examines the role of sampling settings, filter strictness, and dataset size, and compares a text-only teacher channel with an image-based student evaluation to characterize cross-modal transfer of the fine-tuning effect. Findings indicate that surface-safe generated text can carry implicit signals that degrade student safety competence, and that the effect reproduces across random seeds.
